Before ordering: confirm tab arrangement, bearing/rod-end bore, grip stack and locking method. A larger bolt requires compatible bearings and tabs; do not simply enlarge a rod-end bore. Shared arm pickups assume one common bolt. The ideal two-force linkage model does not resolve arm bending from its pushrod bracket. Pivot force-only sizing does not cover its reaction moment. All rows exclude bolt bending, combined tension, fatigue, tab bearing/tear-out and weld checks.

The old sheet lists AN3-12A, AN4-13A and AN5-14A for its tab stacks; these lengths are not transferred to the new geometry. Use a smooth shank through the shear planes and select the dash length after measuring the full stack. The suffix and locking method remain to be specified.

Margin convention: MS = allowable ÷ applied − 1. Negative is a predicted failure; zero is the allowable boundary. Tube checks include yield, ultimate, and Euler buckling with the workbook’s safety factors.

JMX scope: initial selections follow Manufacturing Summary; selectors override them in this browser. JMX margin uses the workbook-derived axial tensile allowable as a screening proxy; verify final rod-end radial ratings, misalignment, threads, bolts, tabs, fatigue, and manufacturer data before release.

Tube plugs & thread engagement

One plug at each end of every linkage tube. JMX selections follow Member Sizing, including browser overrides. Each end carries the full member force.

Proposed engagement starts at the workbook minimum rounded up to whole threads. Edit each end independently; these are design dimensions, not measured installed engagement.

Minimum engagement and estimated mass per plug. All dimensions in inches; weight in pounds.
Corner / memberEndJMX / threadTube OD / IDMinimum engagementProposed engagementEngagement marginInsert radial wallPlug weightCheck
Workbook equations and assumptions

Source: Minimum Thread Engagement, rows 9–11 of Mk11 Susp Linkage Forces (1).xlsx. Thread mapping: JMX3 → 10-32; JMX4 → 1/4-28; JMX5 → 5/16-24.

Tensile area At = π/4 × (d − 0.9743/n)².
Base engagement Le = 2At / [π n D1,max (1/(2n) + 0.57735(d2,min − D1,max))].
Required engagement = 1.5 Le. Proposed default = ceil(required × n) / n, rounded upward to 0.00001 in. Margin = proposed / required − 1.

d is the worksheet external major diameter; n is threads per inch; D1,max is maximum internal minor diameter; d2,min is minimum external pitch diameter. JMX3 retains the sheet’s d = 0.1935 for parity (nominal #10 is 0.190). These source dimensions require confirmation against the selected thread class.

Cap thickness = 0.130; density = 0.284 lb/in³. Cap OD follows tube OD; insert OD follows tube ID. Approximate plug weight = ρπ/4 × [(OD² − d²) × 0.130 + (ID² − d²) × (proposed engagement − 0.130)]. Radial wall = (ID − d)/2.

The weight formula consistently uses annular volumes and current tube dimensions. This corrects the sheet’s inconsistent E17 cap expression, E26 density reference, and old front tube references. Circular mass estimates omit hex flats, thread helix, chamfers and welds.

Engagement is the workbook’s thread-strength criterion, not a load-scaled stripping calculation. Positive radial wall checks geometric clearance only; it does not validate insert strength, minimum machining wall, welds or material-strength mismatch. Verify thread stripping for the actual plug and rod-end materials before manufacture.

Load convention: each vector is applied by the suspension to the chassis. Direct links and the shock are two-force members; the rocker row is an equivalent wrench at the physical pivot-axis midpoint.

Calculation method · embedded configuration

From tire patch to chassis hardpoint

The model follows the load path in the same order the hardware carries it. A six-member rigid-upright solve produces axial linkage forces; the pushrod then drives a rigid rocker, the rocker drives the shock/spring assembly, and equal-and-opposite reactions are collected at the chassis.

These controls also set the 3D viewer. Diagrams use the active geometry and the default 3D orientation in an orthographic projection.

INPUTTire force
WRENCHForce + moment
6 × 6Upright balance
AXIALLink forces
MOMENTRocker + shock
REACTIONChassis loads

01Inputs

Keep load axes and CAD axes explicit

Tire-load and coordinate conventions are read from the embedded configuration.

Fcoordinate = diag(1, 1, 1) Finput
The transform changes basis. It does not move or relabel any hardpoint.
Geometry input

Each member has an outboard application point and an inboard anchor, both in inches.

Load input

Each case supplies Fx, Fy, Fz in lbf and may include an application point or applied moment.

02External load

Reduce the tire load to one wrench

The tire force is transferred to the selected upright reference point. Its moment is the cross product of the offset from that reference and the applied force, plus any directly supplied moment.

W = [ F ; M ]
M = (rtire − rref) × F + Minput

Changing the reference point changes the individual moment numbers but not the physical member-force solution, provided every member moment arm is formed about the same reference.

03Geometry

Represent six ideal axial members

The upright is connected by exactly six independent force directions: tie/toe rod, lower fore, lower aft, upper fore, upper aft, and pushrod. Each is idealized as pin-jointed and carries no bending moment.

ûi = (ranchor,i − rapplication,i) / ‖ranchor,i − rapplication,i‖
Fi = Ni ûi

With the direction defined from upright to chassis, positive N is tension and negative N is compression. Reversing only the stored member direction reverses the scalar sign but leaves the physical vector unchanged.

Model boundary: each fore and aft wishbone leg is treated as its own two-force member. Local A-arm bending, tabs, bolts, rod-end misalignment, compliance, fatigue, and joint friction require separate checks.
04Rigid body

Solve force and moment equilibrium together

Each member contributes one force column and one moment column. The six unknown axial forces satisfy three force equations and three moment equations on the rigid upright.

Ai = [ ûi ; (rapplication,i − rref) × ûi ]

A N = −W

Exactly determined

Six independent member directions produce six unknown axial forces for six equilibrium equations.

Condition check

A large matrix condition number warns that small coordinate changes can cause large force changes.

05Motion ratio

Balance the rocker about its measured axis

The solved push/pull-rod force is applied to the rocker. The shock force is found by balancing only the moment component about the rocker’s rotation axis. The shock chassis pickup remains fixed; only its rocker pickup rotates.

â · [(rrod − rpivot) × Frod + (rshock − rpivot) × Nshockûshock] = 0

Nshock = − momentrod,axis / momentshock,axis per lbf

The pivot reaction closes force equilibrium on the rocker. Reaction moment components not carried by the ideal rotation-axis torque balance are also reported for chassis review.

06Nonlinear pose

Iterate geometry against spring force

Ride-height coordinates are the reference pose. The model preserves the six linkage lengths while allowing three upright translations, three upright rotations, and one rocker rotation. A seventh residual matches calculated shock compression force to spring force.

R = [ ΔL1 … ΔL6 ; (−Nshock − Fride − k Δs) / k ] = 0

A finite-difference Newton iteration solves the seven constraints. Ride-height preload values are read from the embedded configuration.

07Output

Apply equal-and-opposite loads to the chassis

At every direct link anchor, the chassis load is equal and opposite to the member force acting on the suspension. The shock load enters at its fixed chassis pickup. The pushrod is internal to the suspension-plus-rocker free body, so it is not counted again as a chassis interface.

  • Wishbone and tie/toe-rod anchors receive axial link reactions.
  • The shock chassis pickup receives the axial shock reaction.
  • The rocker bearing receives an equivalent force and moment at the physical pivot axis.
  • The maximum-envelope view selects the largest |F| independently at each hardpoint.
08Checks

Verify the solver before trusting the updated model

Mk11 reference workbook audit: the supplied workbook’s cached 6 × 6 matrices and load vectors were solved directly with the Python linear solver. This isolates the algebra from all coordinate, rocker, spring, and four-corner changes. These recorded parity results apply to the Mk11 reference audit, not automatically to another input file.

VerificationResult
Workbook force reproduction, 8 casesmax error 2.63 × 10−7 lbf
Workbook equilibrium residualbelow 3.0 × 10−7
Fixed-geometry force reversalexact sign reversal, 0.0 lbf error
Current model versus workbook maximanot parity

The first three checks verify the equilibrium implementation. The final comparison is intentionally different because the current model uses updated CAD hardpoints, four physical corners, spring-loaded moving geometry, and calculated rather than manually overridden maxima.

Interpretation: a successful equilibrium check proves that the assumed model balances. It does not prove that every hardpoint, tire-force direction, spring preload, or structural idealization matches the physical car. Those inputs still require CAD and test correlation.
